turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
The highest observed rotating-bending fatigue strengths (1000–1190 MPa) form a single, well-populated cluster whose process signature is identical: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Tt=120, TCr=0.5 together with a low-temperature temper (TT=160–200). Inside that cluster the remaining variables (Ct, DT, Dt, QmT and the whole composition vector) already span wide intervals while the target stays above 1000 MPa; consequently a 5 % perturbation of any one coordinate remains inside a high-performing region rather than falling off a sharp peak.

A point lying in the interior of that cluster (rather than at an extreme vertex such as the single 1190 MPa record) is therefore both high-performing and robust:

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=400, DT=850, Dt=30, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.28, Mn=0.70, P=0.015, S=0.015, Ni=0.50, Cr=0.80, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.16, RedRatio=500, dA=0.04, dB=0.005, dC=0.005
